stage1.impression: A clean, evenly lit retail render seen through a shopfront: oak shelves of glowing multicoloured spheres, a blown-out terrazzo plinth, and a pink-white light bar at the back of a long room. It reads as a lamp showroom or a CG archviz still, not a night photograph of a listening bar. The exposure is far too high for night (median about 106), the speckled terrazzo looks like a procedural texture, the light lines look like white LED neon, and the many saturated tints scatter the eye so no single object is the hero. A design magazine would see a generic shop with a bar behind it, not a specific, well-made place.

blocking_9: Frame exposed as night: lum_median 22-50, with pools of light and real dark between them (now 105.6, evenly lit)
The lantern's band reads as warm amber glowing through thick fins, not a pink-white clipped strip (now ΔE2000 26 vs #F0A040, clip 5.2%)
The window plinth is not the brightest thing in the frame (now median 202) and its terrazzo chips are at a believable scale, not coarse speckle
The shelf and back-bar lines read as warm concealed light on oak, not white neon tubes
The lantern is the hero, read at a glance; the tinted Cores support it instead of competing with it
Signs of life: glasses on the counter and table, a record out of its sleeve, a coat or bag
The mullion does not cut the frame near its centre; faint street reflections in the glass make the 'through the shopfront' read
Materials hold up at 1:1: plaster with trowel variation, oak with real grain and end grain, steel with an uneven sheen

defects.what: Overexposed for night: lum_median 105.6, only 28.8% of pixels below 40; reads as daytime or showroom
Lantern band clips (5.19%) and is pink-white (RGB 251/227/221), not amber; reads as a lightbox or signage
Terrazzo window plinth blown to median 202; chips oversized and noisy, a procedural speckle; a hard diagonal shadow streak runs across its top
Shelf LED lines are thin pure-white strips, like neon; shelves too bright (median 137)
Rows of identical spheres in every tint: repeated copies of one model, a rainbow that breaks the one-colour rule
Bar stools stacked in a tight line, overlapping and reading as repeated copies or an intersecting stack
Dark vertical mullion splits the frame just right of centre and cuts through the table
Right plaster wall evenly lit and smooth (median 109.5, p5-p95 only 24-176), no pools, no trowel texture; reads as CG
Slotted oak baffle reads pink-mauve and flat; little falloff (150 to 84 down its height), no graze across the slots
Ceiling is a near-empty dark void with faint stray light streaks; no visible downlight fixtures or beams
Pendants in pink and violet add more saturated colour at the back
No signs of life: no glasses, records, coats or people; an empty showroom

changes.problem: The frame is exposed like a daytime showroom, not a night interior.

change.to: 2.2 (about -1.4 stops), then trim by ±0.2 to land the median

changes.expected: Frame median about 38-45; practicals and lit oak stay legible, the ceiling and corners go dark and the pools of light start to read.

changes.problem: The lantern's band clips and reads pink-white, like a lightbox, instead of an amber glow through thick fins.

change.setting: the lantern's band: emission (and its colour)
change.to: 1.4, colour at about 2000-2200 K (deep amber), so the fins' edges glow and the faces stay below clipping

changes.expected: The band reads amber, the brightest saturated colour at the end of the room, the fins individually legible, with no clipping.

changes.problem: The window plinth is the brightest surface in the frame and pulls the eye away from the room and the lantern.

change.setting: the shop wall spots 30.0 W and the street light on the plinth; terrazzo chip size and ground tone
change.from: 3 x 30.0 W; coarse chips, light ground
change.to: 3 x 12.0 W aimed at the shelves, not the plinth; terrazzo chips about half their current size on a warmer mid-grey ground, honed (rougher)

changes.expected: The plinth sits at mid-tone, a foreground step that frames the room; the Cores on it read as small lamps.

changes.problem: The shelf lines read as white neon tubes and overlight the shelves.

evidence.measured: lum_median 137.1; the line is a pure-white stroke at 1:1 (crop 0,0-450,300)

change.to: 1.8 at 2400 K, the source hidden behind the shelf lip so only the wash on the oak shows

changes.expected: Warm washes down each shelf back with no visible emitter line; the shelves fall to mid-tone.

changes.problem: The room is lit evenly, with no pools of light and no real dark between them.

evidence.measured: right plaster wall lum_median 109.5, p5 24.3 to p95 176.2, flat

change.setting: the route area 0.3 W/m2, the fill 0.06 W/m2, haze
change.to: route 0.1, fill 0.03, haze 0.007/m; keep the counter spots at 14 W and the table spot at 14 W so their pools carry the room

changes.expected: The right wall falls dark between pools; the counter and table read as lit islands; faint beams in the haze under the downlights.

changes.problem: The mullion splits the frame near its centre and the lantern is too small to be the hero.

evidence.measured: a 40 px dark bar at x 830-870 through the table; the band occupies only 465-778 x 262-295

change.to: slide the camera along the glass (about 0.6 m along y) so the mullion falls at the frame edge or out of frame; 40 mm lens, target centred on the lantern's face; keep verticals true

changes.expected: One uninterrupted view down the room with the lantern's band on the upper third; the shop still frames the foreground.

changes.problem: The room is empty, with nothing that says someone was just here.

evidence.measured: the counter and table tops are bare except one small object

change.to: two half-full glasses and a bottle on the counter, a record out of its sleeve and a glass on the shop table, a coat over one stool; break up the stool line with slight rotations

changes.expected: Small highlights on glass under the counter spots; the bar reads as open tonight.

changes.problem: The plaster wall and the oak baffle read smooth and pink, not lime plaster and oiled oak under 2700 K light.

evidence.measured: baffle RGB 167/127/110, a mauve-pink cast; right wall a near-uniform smooth surface

change.setting: white_balance_tint, plaster and oak finish within their kind
change.from: tint 1.0; smooth plaster; pale pink oak
change.to: tint toward green until the oak reads honey-brown, not mauve; lime plaster with trowel variation and soft mottling; oak oiled a step darker and warmer

changes.expected: Warm brown oak and warm grey plaster; the only saturated colour is the lamps' and the band's.

out_of_scope.request: Fewer tints on the Cores and Hemispheres, or one tint only
out_of_scope.why: EARF's products and their tints are fixed as placed; the rainbow breaks the one-colour rule and is the main thing holding the frame back from 8.5

out_of_scope.request: Fewer identical spheres on the shelves
out_of_scope.why: The shop's shelves and the products on them are fixed

out_of_scope.request: Rearranging the stools along the counter
out_of_scope.why: May be part of the drawn plan; if the stools are props, space them about 600 mm apart
